conflict_topics: who prepares meals on which nights
eating together vs. separate meal prep
dialogue_quality_notes: Problem stated clearly by D with a concrete constraint ('no meat, nothing fried for me').
Participants gave concrete reasons for difficulty (A: lack of experience; C: doesn't cook vegetarian/non-fried).
B proposed a practical, split-responsibility compromise that produced acceptance.
Acceptance and the remaining condition (D wanting to eat together) are explicitly stated and echoed.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent B proposed that Agents A and C cook for the three other housemates on their nights and that Agent D prepare their own compliant meals on those nights. Agent C accepted ('That works for me.'), Agent D accepted with the condition of still eating together ('I can make my own food on those nights, sure. As long as we all still eat together at the same time?'), and Agent A explicitly agreed ('Yeah, that's fine. The main thing is that we all eat together.'). Thus A and C adjusted to cook for three people on their nights and D adjusted by preparing separate food while maintaining shared mealtimes; no additional compensation or third-party intervention was requested.
position_change_notes: Agent C moved from 'I don't cook vegetarian food' to accepting to cook for the group on their night ('That works for me.').

Agent A moved from 'I don't really cook anything without meat' to explicitly agreeing to the compromise and prioritizing shared mealtimes ('Yeah, that's fine. The main thing is that we all eat together.').
Agent D moved from requesting a rota change (needs no meat/no fried) to offering to prepare their own compliant meals while still eating together ('I can make my own food on those nights...').
Agent B remained a facilitator, proposing the compromise that resolved the conflict.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D announces a temporary strict diet for a month ('The doctor's put me on a strict diet for the next month. It's a liver thing. So... no meat, nothing fried for me.') — informational only, no incompatibility expressed yet.

Agent A says this is a problem for their night ('That's a problem for my night, then. I don't really cook anything without meat.') while Agent B says it's not a problem on theirs — a mild substantive disagreement about rota feasibility emerges.

Agent C joins in saying it's also a problem for their night ('It's a problem for my night, too.'), increasing the scope of incompatibility between D's dietary needs and the existing rota/cooking habits.

C clarifies inability to cook vegetarian/non-fried meals ('I don't cook vegetarian food. I don't know what to make that isn't fried.'), and B offers a practical suggestion to D ('Agent D, maybe you could just tell them what to make.') — problem remains but a proposed aid appears.

D offers to suggest dishes ('I can suggest some simple things, if that helps?'), but A notes a deeper barrier ('I've never cooked a meal without meat, I wouldn't know where to start.') — the incompatibility is still unresolved.

B proposes a concrete compromise: A and C cook for three people and D makes their own food on those nights ('Why don't Agent A and Agent C just cook for the three of us on their nights, and Agent D, you make something for yourself then?') — a move toward resolution though not yet accepted by all.

C accepts the proposal ('That works for me.') and D agrees to make their own food while requesting to still eat together ('I can make my own food on those nights, sure. As long as we all still eat together at the same time? I'd still like to be part of the dinners.') — core compromise largely accepted, but A hasn't yet agreed explicitly.

Agent A explicitly agrees to the arrangement ('Yeah, that's fine. The main thing is that we all eat together.') and C echoes agreement — the incompatible demands are settled: A and C will cover cooking for the group and D will prepare their own food but eat with everyone.
D expresses gratitude and no new issues are raised ('Great. Thanks, everyone. I appreciate it.').

substantive_insights: The core tension was a medical dietary restriction colliding with a pre-existing rota where cooks habitually use meat or frying.
Skill/experience (A's unfamiliarity with vegetarian cooking) was as important a constraint as willingness.
A practical compromise preserved social goals (shared mealtimes) while separating the practical task of meal preparation.
